quest.title: Unknown Star
quest.description: Katheryne of the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild seems to have something to tell you.
quest.rewards_formatted: Fading Star's Might x40, Primogem x60, Mora x30000

talks.objective: Go to the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild and look for Katheryne

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler. You couldn't have come at a better time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean? Has something bad happened?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I'm afraid so. It's quite serious... We need all the help from our adventurers that we can get.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: So, I have an extremely urgent commission for you, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... That does sound pretty serious...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Truth be told, we have never encountered anything like this before.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The Adventurers' Guild is currently stretched beyond capacity. We are relying on our members across the land to rally together and support the relief effort at this trying time.

choices.text: I will surely do my part.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: One moment, safety must come first...

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Katheryne! Vassal of the Immernachtreich, do mine ears deceive me, or didst thou cry out mine holy name in earnest supplication not one moment ago?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Ah, you've arrived.

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: A pleasure to meet you again, Katheryne.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Did that raven just speak!?

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Haha, nice to meet you too, my friend... Though I'm sure you must have seen phenomena far stranger than myself before?

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: My loyal subjects, I see your faces are filled with fear and trepidation at the vile and villainous evils that once again seek, albeit in vain, to disturb the peace and tranquility of our beloved Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Traveler, allow me to introduce Miss Fischl, a senior member of the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Fischl, Oz, this is the Traveler of whom I have spoken to you previously.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Oh? You are the Traveler? Hmm... One finds the look in your eyes to be most agreeable.

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius, and travel companion Paimon, we are honored to meet you both. We have heard much about you.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Traveler, do you also mean to confront these cryptic crystals of darkness and doom?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Cry—Crystic cryptals of... doomness and... What?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Katheryne, is that the same thing you were talking about?

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: I believe that mein Fräulein does indeed refer to the <color=#00E1FFFF>meteorite strike</color>.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The Adventurers' Guild has so far been unable to ascertain the cause of the meteor shower, or the precise side effects of the meteorites. Hence, we recommend that adventurers travel in pairs for safety.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Traveler, Fischl, please look out for one another on your journey, and exercise extreme caution at all times.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Hm. Very well then. You have always been a pious vassal, Katheryne, and thus I shall acquiesce to your heartfelt plea for mine assistance.

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Rejoice! For to join the Prinzessin der Verurteilung on her majestic mission for but a fleeting moment is surely cause for an eternity of elation!

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: This young lady is my master, Princess Fischl. She hails from a world beyond known as Immernachtreich. I am mein Fräulein's humble familiar, Oz the Raven.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... That all sounds very impressive...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #My name's Paimon, and {NICKNAME}'s a traveler. We look forward to working with you!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: In time, you will understand... The more time you spend with Miss Fischl, the clearer everything will become...

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: Hmph, blind to the glory of the Immernachtreich, realm of everlasting night... Though, one could hardly expect more from a lowly traveler... Hence, it is not blasphemy, but ignorance, that be the cause of this transgression. One will therefore show clemency.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Clemency?

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Mein Fräulein means to say: "Hello."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: These guys are the weirdest double act Paimon's ever seen... The girl sounds strange enough as it is, but every time her pet bird talks, it gets even weirder...

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: I am sure that you must have many questions. Perhaps we can walk — or indeed fly — and talk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and that's another thing... What's all this about traveling in pairs? This is clearly a party of four!

choices.text: "Immernachtreich..."? Never heard of that place before.
Thanks for the info! I'd better hop to it~

talks.objective: Check out the situation at Springvale

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're in Springvale now. Katheryne said that this is the closest impact site to the city.

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: The situation looks even worse than we imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So many people have fainted.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ring the bells, sound the trumpets, for the day of judgment is upon us! Rejoice, all ye who cry out for salvation, for the Prinzessin der Verurteilung has come!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This princess lady seems really enthusiastic.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Dear mortals, in this dark hour, your Prinzessin permits you to forgo the usual etiquette and simply relay your account of the matter at hand forthrightly.

dialogues.speaker: Joyce
dialogues.text: ...Excuse me? Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: We come in peace, good sir. We were just hoping that you could reveal whatever you know about this poor victim's situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, wait! Stop, let Paimon explain... We're from the Adventurers' Guild. They commissioned us to come here and investigate after the meteor shower.

dialogues.speaker: Joyce
dialogues.text: Oh, I see. Well, last night, this fellow touched the meteorite, and then he fainted just moments later.

dialogues.speaker: Joyce
dialogues.text: So, however you plan to conduct your investigation, I implore you: Do not, under any circumstances, touch the meteorites with your bare hands.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: What ridiculous remonstration is this? Is one not under the divine protection of one's Edelstein der Dunkelheit, and thus impervious to the trifling threat posed by this petty piece of black crystal?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: On the contrary, mein Fräulein, wise is the princess who is receptive to the sound advice offered by her subjects.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Is that so... Very well then, one shall proceed as advised.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That goes for you, too, {NICKNAME}! Wise is the adventurer who is receptive to the sound advice offered by smart people!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehehehe, Paimon never gets to talk like that! Oh, Paimon could get used to it, though...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: You dare to parrot the parlance of the Prinzessin!? Hmph! What could one hope to comprehend of the lamenting of a thousand dying worlds with the sagacity of a mere mortal?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Perhaps it is better that you remain in blissful ignorance, for the burden of fate borne by the Prinzessin der Verurteilung would surely be too much for thy shoulders.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please lead the way, O fair Princess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, another victim!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Pray tell, O Knight, what tragedy befell this unfortunate subject of mine?

dialogues.speaker: Adler
dialogues.text: Um... He— He's been sleeping all day and shows no signs of waking up.

response.speaker: Adler
response.text: He did. And now he's fast asleep, occasionally he also sleep-talks.

response.speaker: Unconscious Victim
response.text: Can't go on... n—need to rest...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What's going on? Why is he saying that?

response.speaker: Fischl
response.text: His dark dream harbors a forbidden fruit, poised between the jaws of a ferocious beast... Woe betide the weak should they peer into its eyes, as black as a moonless midnight, for they shall surely be lured into the abyss...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you mean... There's something luring him in his dream?

response.speaker: Oz
response.text: Though we have no evidence to prove it, mein Fräulein's intuition has never failed her before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Well, let's keep investigating anyway!

choices.text: Are there any other symptoms besides the deep sleep?

response.speaker: Adler
response.text: Not that I've seen so far, although occasionally he talks in his sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: Greetings, I am Sister Edna. I am here to nurse the sick.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: State your name at once, you heinous heathen of nefarious nightmares!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: My apologies, mein Fräulein was not addressing you... This man lying on the ground — has he spoken at all?

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: I believe he said something about having to get back to work...

dialogues.speaker: Hartman
dialogues.text: The wine... The wine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So he works in the wine business?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: He seems to be sleeping deeply indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: This is no ordinary dream... This man... he has been cursed!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't you just wake him up?

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: I have tried. He awoke once, for a brief moment, but quickly lapsed back into sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Did he tell you anything while he was awake?

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: He said he dreamed he was on top of a mountain, and it was very cold there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Mountain, cold... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: This has the trappings of a cruel, cold curse by a mountain-dwelling demon... Alas! One fears these demons have descended from their icy peaks and now covet the domain of the spring fairy!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: This is a most grave state of affairs... But fear not, for damnation is mine to dispense—

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt you, folks — do you have a moment to spare?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey, Draff! What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: It's... I—I can hardly get the words out...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: One of the <color=#00E1FFFF>meteorites</color> struck the <color=#00E1FFFF>hill behind our village</color>. <color=#00E1FFFF>Allan</color> told everyone he was going to go see it for himself... And then, sure enough, he just ran off.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: You've seen how dangerous these confounded meteorites are. I'm afraid something may have happened to him... Could you come with me to find him and bring him back?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so... Big blazing rocks fall out of the sky, and all Allan's worried about is missing out on the action!?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Exactly! Once we get that rascal back safely, he's due for the scolding of a lifetime, if you ask me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon could not agree more! Let's go find that rascal and drag him back by the ears!

talks.objective: Head to the hill to look for Allan
Rescue Allan from the monsters surrounding him

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Phew! I thought I was going to die here...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: You fool! What were you thinking, gallivanting off on your own at a time like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: I—I'm sorry! I'll never do it again!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: I sincerely apologize for the trouble Allan has caused for you all. I will make absolutely sure that he learns his lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, next time you think about doing something stupid, think again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The meteorite is just over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's gonna go take a closer loo— Huh? Princess, your <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color> is <color=#00E1FFFF>flashing</color>!

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Oh? Could it be, perchance, that mine Edelstein der Dunkelheit portends the certain demise of this unholy hex of cold?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe...? What kind of things does your Vision react to, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: The profoundest of enigmas... the whispered secrets of the stars... unholy hexes of demon bones... and—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whaaaat? Why do you have to talk so funny all the time, Paimon doesn't understand!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: Our apologies, mein Fräulein is not well-versed in the parlance of the common folk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooooh, so that's what you're for? To translate?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: I fear you misunderstand — I am no translator, but a humble conveyor of mein Fräulein's royal will. I would venture that what her <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color> is reacting to in this vicinity is, quite simply, <color=#00E1FFFF>elemental energy</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ahem, thank you, Oz. Those whose minds are muddled by the mundane matters of this woeful world are unable to fathom my noble intent as swiftly as thou art...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, there's elemental energy in the meteorite? And your Vision flashes in response to it?

choices.text: With a Vision, can you trace the elemental energy back to its source?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks... probably yes? Anyway, no harm in giving it a try! Let's look for <color=#00E1FFFF>shards of meteorite</color> using Fischl's <color=#00E1FFFF>Vision</color> — clearing them away will help make the area less dangerous.

choices.text: Shouldn't the source of the energy also respond in like fashion?

talks.objective: Clear out the meteorite shards on the hill (0/2)
Clear out the meteorite shards on the hill (1/2)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That seems to be the last of them. Do you think getting rid of them will help make things better for the Springvale villagers?

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: The question is, are these shards of meteorite, which are infused with elemental energy, the true source of the calamity, or not?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Verily, I say, these meteorites are surely the source of the nefarious nightmares that assail my subjects! This I swear on my very sovereignty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Shall we check in with the villagers, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's do that!

talks.objective: Return to Springvale to check on the victims

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Edna! We got rid of the meteorite up on the hill behind the village. How are the victims doing now? Any better?

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: Bless you! Thanks to your efforts, two of the victims have already awoken.

dialogues.speaker: Hartman
dialogues.text: Ugh... I'm so sleepy... *yawn*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great, so it did work!

dialogues.speaker: Edna
dialogues.text: I do hope you are able to dispose of the rest of the <color=#00E1FFFF>meteorites</color> around the village...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then everyone else will wake up, too!

dialogues.speaker: Oz
dialogues.text: This is wonderful news, it gladdens the heart.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Haha, it is most gladdening, indeed. Yet the news that I would be attending to this matter in person was surely the only guarantee that my faithful subjects ever needed of a felicitous outcome!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you just woke up, right? What were you dreaming about while you were asleep?

dialogues.speaker: Hartman
dialogues.text: All I remember is that it was cold... I was walking along a <color=#00E1FFFF>mountain</color> path... In the ice and snow, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Just hiking in the mountains? Or were you supposed to have a destination?

dialogues.speaker: Hartman
dialogues.text: Ah, I really don't know... In my dream, it felt like... I wasn't in full control of my actions.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Then thou wert surely cursed, I say! O, wretched scourge upon this land...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A curse? Could it really be?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, whatever the case, what we do know is that getting rid of the meteorite shards is helping. So, c'mon guys, we need to redouble our efforts!
